verified_claims_summary: Google News officially states that algorithms personalize sections based on user settings, interests, and past activity on Google services and YouTube, and that users can follow or unfollow topics and sources, request more or fewer similar stories, and hide sources. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/googlenews/answer/9010862?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en&utm_source=openai))

The Reuters Institute’s 2016 U.S. survey reported that 59% worried personalized news could cause them to miss challenging or different viewpoints, while also finding that personalized recommendations were viewed favorably by some respondents. ([reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/archive/essays/2016/people-want-personalised-recommendations/?utm_source=openai))

The Bakshy, Messing, and Adamic Facebook study found slightly less cross-cutting content after algorithmic ranking than was potentially available through friends’ shares, while users’ own click choices had a stronger limiting effect. ([education.biu.ac.il](https://education.biu.ac.il/sites/education/files/shared/science-2015-bakshy-1130-2.pdf))

The article’s statement about short-term tests finding no measurable change in some political attitudes is supported by 2020 Facebook and Instagram feed experiments and the 2020 Facebook like-minded-source intervention. Those studies also state that their durations and designs could not establish the effects of cumulative exposure over many years. ([csmapnyu.org](https://csmapnyu.org/research/academic-research/how-do-social-media-feed-algorithms-affect-attitudes-and-behavior-in-an-election-campaign))

The description of ranking systems as using behavioral signals such as clicks, likes, shares, and search history, while being adjustable to business goals such as engagement and advertising revenue, is consistent with the Congressional Research Service’s description of social-media algorithms. ([everycrsreport.com](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R46662.html?utm_source=openai))
